title: Hopping below zero on a number line
examples: How do negative numbers work on a number line?
Is minus 5 bigger or smaller than minus 2?

explain.say: Imagine a cold morning in Beijing. It is 3 degrees, and by night it gets 7 degrees colder. Where do you land? Watch the hops on the number line. You start at 3, go past zero, and land on minus 4.

draw.text: Hopping below zero on a number line

explain.say: Now let us go the other way. Adding means hopping right. You start at minus 4 and hop 6 to the right. See how you cross zero and land on 2? Each hop right makes the number bigger.
Taking away means hopping left. Start at minus 2 and take away 3. You land on minus 5. Look: minus 5 is further left, so it is the smaller number. Is minus 5 degrees warmer or colder than minus 2?
Negative numbers are all around you. A freezing night, a diver under the sea, money you owe. Look at the below zero group on the board. Can you think of one more thing that goes below zero?

Well done, you can hop both ways now! Last one: start at minus 10 and hop 15 right. You land on 5. Here is a wow: the shore of the Dead Sea is about 430 metres below sea level, the lowest land on Earth. Can you work out minus 10 plus 25?

faq.q: Is minus 5 bigger or smaller than minus 2?
faq.a: Minus 5 is smaller. It sits further left on the number line, and numbers get smaller as you go left. Minus 5 degrees is colder than minus 2.

faq.q: What happens when you subtract past zero?
faq.a: You keep hopping left, past zero, into the negative numbers. So 3 minus 7 lands on minus 4.
asks: Can you take a bigger number from a smaller one?

faq.a: Anything measured the other way from a starting point: minus 12 degrees on a cold night, a diver 3 metres under the water, or money you owe.
asks: Where are negative numbers used in real life?
Why do we need negative numbers?

faq.q: How do you add a negative number?
faq.a: Adding a negative is the same as taking away. So 5 plus minus 3 means hop 3 to the left, and you land on 2.

faq.q: What is the gap between minus 3 and 4?
faq.a: Count the hops. It is 3 hops from minus 3 up to zero, then 4 more hops to 4. So the gap is 7.
asks: How do you find the difference between a negative and a positive number?

facts: The shore of the Dead Sea, between Jordan and Israel, is the lowest land on Earth, roughly 430 metres below sea level.
In 628 CE the Indian mathematician Brahmagupta wrote rules for negative numbers, which he called debts.

quiz.say: Start at 2 on the number line and hop 6 to the left. Where do you land?
quiz.why: From 2 it takes 2 hops to reach zero, then 4 more hops left lands on minus 4.

wrong.1: 4 is the gap left over, but you forgot to cross zero.
wrong.2: Minus 8 adds the 2 instead of starting from it.

quiz.say: Which temperature is colder: minus 8 degrees or minus 3 degrees?
quiz.why: Minus 8 is further left on the number line, so it is smaller and colder.

wrong.1: Minus 3 is closer to zero, so it is warmer.
wrong.2: They are 5 degrees apart on the number line.
